0.0.n: Points to something distant from both speaker and listener, or something they both know.

0.1.n: Names the place the speaker wants to cross.

0.2.n: Marks the space crossed with 越える, rather than something acted upon.

0.3.n: The て-form of 越える links crossing the sea to going to see someone.

0.5.n: A familiar way to address someone, fitting the intimate tone here.

0.6.n: Marks 君 as the person the speaker wants to meet.

0.7.n: 会う becomes 会い before に to express the purpose of going.

0.8.n: Follows 会い to mark meeting as the purpose of going.

0.9.n: 行く becomes 行きたい with たい, expressing the speaker’s desire in a plain, non-polite form.

1.0.n: A casual, masculine way to refer to oneself.

1.2.n: This is a person’s name, written in katakana.

1.3.n: Links ユンスル to こと, making the person the focus of the unfinished thought.

1.4.n: In ユンスルのこと, it refers broadly to Yun-seul; the speaker trails off before stating any feelings.

2.0.n: ミリ is a common shortening of ミリメートル, a unit of length.

2.1.n: Links the measurement to 恋, presenting it as a description of the love.

2.2.n: Refers specifically to romance or being in love, rather than affection in general.

0.lit: That sea across, crossing, you with meeting in order to, want to go.
0.tip: A verb’s stem plus に行く means going to do something; 会いにいきたい adds the desire to go.

1.tip: The unfinished sentence leaves the speaker’s feelings unstated; のこと makes Yun-seul the focus.

2.tip: This title-like phrase uses の to connect a measurement to romantic love.
